Excess Demand: Existence and Uniqueness

Measure how much extra people want at each price and draw it as a curve. Where the curve crosses zero is the equilibrium. A positive excess means buyers want more than sellers offer. A negative excess means the opposite. In a well-behaved economy the curve crosses zero exactly once. But that is a gift, not a guarantee. Switch the mode and you can watch it cross three times. For example, call out 🍞 bread prices from 100 up to 1,000 won. Priced too cheap, 🧑 people line up to buy. Priced too dear, loaves pile up unsold. Only at the right price is there no line and no leftovers. That price is the equilibrium.
